playlist.playlist_title: Kali Linux Complete Course 2027 | Learn Ethical Hacking & Penetration Testing From Scratch #kali #linux #cybersecurity #kalilinux
playlist.description:
🔥 Want to learn ethical hacking but don't know where to start? This is the Kali Linux Complete Course 2026, a free, step-by-step series that takes you from installing Kali Linux to running real penetration testing tools like Nmap, Metasploit, Burp Suite, Wireshark, Nikto, and John the Ripper.

No prior experience needed. If you can install an app, you can follow this course. Every chapter builds on the last, so start from Chapter 1 and work your way through.

👉 SUBSCRIBE and turn on notifications so you never miss a new chapter: https://www.youtube.com/@EINITIAL24/

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
📚 WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

✅ MODULE 1: Kali Linux Setup
• What is Kali Linux and why do security professionals use it
• Installing Kali Linux on VirtualBox, VMware, and bare metal
• Setting up a safe hacking lab on your own computer
• Updating, configuring, and customizing Kali Linux

✅ MODULE 2: Linux Fundamentals for Hackers
• Linux command line basics
• File system structure and permissions
• Users, groups, and privilege management
• Package management, services, and processes
• Bash scripting basics for automation

✅ MODULE 3: Networking for Ethical Hackers
• IP addresses, ports, protocols, and the OSI model
• TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP, and how data moves across networks
• Staying anonymous with Proxychains and Tor
• Surface web vs deep web vs dark web explained

✅ MODULE 4: Information Gathering and Reconnaissance
• Passive and active reconnaissance
• Footprinting, OSINT, and DNS enumeration
• Network scanning with Nmap
• Finding live hosts, open ports, and running services

✅ MODULE 5: Vulnerability Analysis
• How vulnerability scanning works
• Using Searchsploit to find public exploits
• Web server scanning with Nikto
• Reading scan results and prioritizing risks

✅ MODULE 6: Exploitation Basics
• Introduction to Metasploit Framework
• Understanding payloads, exploits, and sessions
• Safe, legal exploitation inside your own lab

✅ MODULE 7: Password Attacks
• How password cracking works
• Wordlists, hashes, and brute-force methods
• John the Ripper, Hashcat, and Hydra
• How to protect your accounts from these attacks

✅ MODULE 8: Wireless Security
• How Wi-Fi security works (WEP, WPA, WPA2, WPA3)
• Wireless testing with Aircrack-ng
• Defending your own network against common attacks

✅ MODULE 9: Web Application Security
• OWASP Top 10 explained for beginners
• Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), SQL Injection, and more
• Intercepting and analyzing traffic with Burp Suite
• Packet analysis with Wireshark

❓ FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Is Kali Linux good for beginners?
Yes, if you learn it step by step. This series starts with installation and Linux basics before touching any hacking tools.

Is ethical hacking legal?
Ethical hacking is legal when you have written permission from the owner of the system. Practice only in your own lab or on platforms built for learning.

Do I need to know programming?
No. Basic scripting is introduced gradually and nothing here requires prior coding experience.

How long does it take to learn Kali Linux?
With regular practice, most beginners are comfortable with the fundamentals in 2–3 months.

Can this course help me get a cybersecurity job?
It builds the practical foundation that entry-level roles and certifications expect. Pair it with hands-on labs like TryHackMe and Hack The Box.

videos.title: How to Perform an Attack Using BeEF (Hooked Browser Modules Explained) | Kali Linux Chapter 76
videos.description:
Chapter 76 of our Complete Kali Linux Series! Building on Chapter 75, where we set up BeEF and hooked our first test browser, this chapter goes deeper into what you can actually do with a hooked browser — BeEF's built-in command modules.

In this video, you'll learn:

A quick recap of hooking a browser with BeEF (for anyone jumping in fresh)
Navigating the BeEF control panel and understanding the hooked browser details panel
Using social engineering modules (e.g., fake prompts) to demonstrate how a hooked session can manipulate the page a user sees
Gathering browser/system information modules — what a hooked session reveals about the target
Using a persistence module to demonstrate how a hook can survive page navigation
Chaining a BeEF module with a Metasploit exploit for a deeper session
Reviewing logs of everything captured during the demo session
Why script-blocking extensions, CSP headers, and updated browsers are the primary defenses against this entire attack class

While Chapter 75 focused on getting a hook, this chapter focuses entirely on using one — the practical command modules and what they demonstrate about client-side risk.

This chapter is performed entirely against a browser owned and controlled by the presenter in an isolated lab environment.

This is part of our Complete Kali Linux Course, covering everything from installation to advanced ethical hacking techniques using tools like Nmap, Wireshark, Aircrack-ng, Metasploit, and Burp Suite. Follow along chapter by chapter for a structured, beginner-friendly path into cybersecurity.

Using BeEF against browsers or systems you don't own or don't have explicit written authorization to test is illegal and can carry serious criminal penalties.

videos.title: Honeypots Explained — How Security Teams Trap Attackers | Kali Linux Course Chapter 73 #kali #linux
videos.description:
Chapter 73 of our Complete Kali Linux Series! After several chapters focused on offense, this chapter shifts to the defensive side of security: honeypots — decoy systems designed to attract, detect, and study attackers.

In this video, you'll learn:

What a honeypot is and how it differs from a normal production system
Low-interaction vs high-interaction honeypots — trade-offs and use cases
Common honeypot types: server honeypots, client honeypots, malware honeypots, honeynets
Why organizations deploy honeypots (early warning, threat intel, distraction/decoy, research)
Setting up a basic honeypot tool in a lab environment
Monitoring and logging connections/attempts made against the honeypot
Analyzing captured attacker activity to understand attack patterns
Legal and ethical considerations when deploying honeypots, including on your own network
How honeypots tie back into everything covered so far — the sniffing, scanning, and exploitation techniques from an attacker's perspective now viewed from the defender's side

This chapter is a good checkpoint in the series: understanding how defenders detect the very techniques we've been practicing gives a fuller, more balanced view of real-world security.

videos.description:
Chapter 72 of our Complete Kali Linux Series! With the Metasploit basics covered in the last chapter, it's time to run our first real exploit — a classic buffer overflow attack against an intentionally vulnerable target.

In this video, you'll learn:

What a buffer overflow is at a conceptual level (writing past allocated memory to overwrite execution flow)
Why buffer overflows can let an attacker redirect a program to run their own code

Using Nmap to identify the vulnerable service and version
Searching Metasploit for a matching exploit module
Configuring the exploit (RHOST, RPORT, target options)

Launching the exploit and gaining a session on the target
Basic post-exploitation: confirming access and exploring the compromised session
Why patching, input validation, and modern memory protections (ASLR, DEP) make buffer overflows harder to exploit today

videos.title: How to Crack WPA/WPA2 WiFi Passwords Using Aircrack-ng | Kali Linux Chapter 69 | 2026 #kali #linux
videos.description:
Chapter 69 of our Complete Kali Linux Series! After cracking WEP in the last chapter, we now move to the far more common (and more challenging) protocol: WPA/WPA2. This chapter walks through the full process of capturing a handshake and attempting to crack it.

In this video, you'll learn:

Why WPA/WPA2 is much stronger than WEP (no more simple IV collection)
Putting your adapter into monitor mode and scanning targets with airodump-ng
Capturing the 4-way handshake from a target network
Using a deauth attack to force a client to reconnect and speed up handshake capture
Verifying you actually captured a valid handshake
Cracking the handshake offline using a wordlist with aircrack-ng
Why wordlist quality/size matters and where crackable passwords typically come from
Introducing faster alternatives (hashcat with GPU cracking) for tougher passwords — teased for a future chapter
Why a strong, unique WiFi password defeats this entire attack

Why WEP is considered broken and insecure (a quick refresher on its weaknesses)

Scanning for nearby WEP-secured networks using airodump-ng
Capturing IVs (initialization vectors) from a target network
Using packet injection / fake authentication to speed up IV collection (aireplay-ng)
Cracking the WEP key once enough IVs are captured with aircrack-ng
Verifying the cracked key by connecting to the test network
Why WEP cracking is fast and easy compared to WPA/WPA2 — and why WEP was deprecated
